mods:mods.mods:abstract: This article develops a novel functionalized meso-adsorbent for selecting, detecting, and removing two different types of metals Li(I) from alkali metals and Mn(II) ions from transition metals, from wastewater. The new meso-adsorbent (MNN) synthesized through functional immobilization of 2-nitroso-1-naphthol (NN) into mesoporous silica monoliths. The Mn(II) and Li(I) complexes with N and O functional groups in the ligand optimized the colour formation and adsorption confirming the formation of [M(MNN)2] M = Mn(II) and Li(I) complexes. The MNN showed fast adsorption and very good separation of Mn(II) and Li(I) from aqueous solution. FTIR analysis data and UV–Vis spectroscopy confirmed that the 2-nitroso-1-naphthol ligand behaves as a bidentate ligand coordinated with the Mn(II) and Li(I) ions via the O atom and the terminal O atom of the NO group. The MNN adsorbent was tested well in different ranges of acidic media for detecting the Mn(II) and Li(I). The influence of pH on the selectivity and sensitivity of the synthesized complexes was also examined after Mn(II) and Li(I) ions addition under fixed conditions. Moreover, the structure of the meso-adsorbent material has a great possibility of being used in detecting and removing simultaneously metal ion selection from wastewater, and it can be used in wastewater treatment efficiently.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Civil infrastructure systems demand frequent, reliable, and cost-effective structural health monitoring (SHM) systems to ensure public safety and serviceability. However, conventional inspection methods based on manual visual surveys and fixed sensing systems are often labor-intensive, costly, time-consuming, and difficult to implement for large-scale or inaccessible structures. In response to these limitations, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones, have emerged as a promising solution for rapid, non-contact, and data-driven infrastructure assessment. The aim of this paper is to provide a comprehensive state-of-the-art review of smart drone technologies for SHM of civil infrastructure and to critically evaluate their capabilities, challenges, and future prospects. A systematic review of the literature was conducted, covering UAV platforms, sensing technologies, autonomous navigation systems, data acquisition strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based damage assessment methods, including computer vision, deep learning, and multi-sensor data fusion techniques. The review reveals that recent advances in UAV hardware and AI-driven analytics have significantly enhanced the accuracy, efficiency, and automation of defect detection, condition assessment, and infrastructure monitoring across bridges, buildings, pavements, heritage structures, and dams. Nevertheless, challenges related to flight endurance, navigation in complex environments, data reliability, real-time processing, regulatory constraints, and large-scale deployment remain significant barriers to widespread implementation. Furthermore, the review identifies current research gaps and emerging trends toward autonomous, collaborative, and intelligent UAV-based monitoring systems. The findings provide valuable guidance for researchers and practitioners seeking to develop next-generation smart drone solutions for resilient and sustainable infrastructure management.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The attitude control of quadrotors is a challenging problem due to its inherent integrating dynamics. This dynamics leads to marginal stability and complicates the design of controllers. This work presents an adaptive single neuron proportional-derivative (ASNPD) controller for quadrotor attitude regulation. The suggested method enhances the traditional single-neuron PD (SNPD) structure by incorporating a bounded nonlinear adaptive mechanism that dynamically modifies the neuron gain based on the current tracking error. Therefore, the controller can deliver larger corrective control actions during the transient response while minimizing the excessive control effort as the error approaches zero. The proposed approach maintains the simplicity and minimal computational processing demands of the single-neuron framework. This makes it appropriate for real-time applications with limited computational power. The performance of the ASNPD controller is experimentally validated utilizing a quadrotor test bench for the yaw-axis attitude control issue. Real-time findings indicate that the proposed controller outperforms the classical SNPD controller in tracking performance while exerting approximately equivalent control effort. From a numerical point of view, ASNPD reduces the integral squared error by around 76.8% in comparison to SNPD. This is an important improvement for applications where accurate tracking is required.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The hot mix asphalt (HMA) production consumes a lot of energy, which in turn generates a large carbon footprint. This study examined the environmental impact of warm mix asphalt (WMA) incorporated with Cup Lump Rubber (CLR), Evotherm additive (EVO), and Palm Oil Fuel Ash (POFA), which are all eco-friendly materials. Four asphalt mixtures were studied: (i) Neat Bitumen (NB), (ii) NB + CLR, (iii) NB + CLR + EVO, (iv) NB + CLR + EVO + POFA. The mixtures were prepared in a lab under standard temperature, and real-time gas emissions were measured (O2, CO2, NO2, SO2, NOn) in a 300-s mixing time. The highest CO2 (1.78 kg/ton) and SO2 (0.48 g/ton) emissions were recorded at high temperatures of 180 °C for NB + CLR. NO2 and SO2 emissions were reduced through Evotherm, and when POFA was used for further modification, SO2 was reduced by an additional 33.2%. These improvements are attributed to lower production temperatures and POFA’s pozzolanic interaction, which neutralizes acid gases. The combined use of WMA technology and waste-derived additives provides a practical route to low-emission asphalt production.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Many modern data sets contain sequences of short regression profiles collected over time, where departures from stability are small, persistent, and difficult to separate from routine variation. This paper proposes a mixed memory procedure for monitoring linear profiles, denoted, that jointly tracks the intercept, the slope, and the error variance in a model with a coded explanatory variable. The method combines exponential smoothing with simple one sided accumulation recursions, which improves sensitivity to gradual changes while keeping componentwise interpretation. The main contribution is a simulation-based design strategy that calibrates control limits to a target in control average run length using projected Robbins Monro updates. This calibration step is a stochastic approximation routine that works with Monte Carlo estimates and adapts the limits through stable, low-cost iterations, which makes the design practical when closed-form limits are unavailable. A unified scaling places all charting statistics on a common unit control limit, which simplifies comparison across components and across competing designs. Performance is studied using run length summaries and domain averaged efficiency criteria over ranges of location and scale shifts, with comparisons to standard profile charts based on Shewhart, exponentially weighted moving average, and cumulative sum ideas under matched false alarm protection. An interactive Shiny application (Application available at https://linearprofiles.shinyapps.io/MEC3/) implements the full workflow, including calibration, simulation experiments, and exportable reports for reproducible use. A data example with 225 profiles illustrates earlier signaling under small sustained departures while maintaining the intended false alarm control.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Ni(II) and Cu(II) mixed-ligand complexes derived from 2-aminothiophenol and thiourea were synthesized by sequential ethanolic reflux and evaluated as corrosion inhibitors for steel in 0.5 M HCl. The products were characterized using elemental analysis, molar conductivity, FT-IR, UV–Vis spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, Cu(II) ESR, thermogravimetric analysis, and density functional theory calculations. The recalculated elemental composition, spectroscopic data, reported qualitative magnetic behavior, and DFT coordination-core models are collectively consistent with four-coordinate structures, with square-planar environments proposed for both metal centers. The Ni(II) product is reported as diamagnetic, consistent with a low-spin d⁸ configuration, whereas Cu(II) is paramagnetic; for Cu(II), g∥ = 2.22 and g⊥ = 2.07 are consistent with a predominantly d(x²−y²) ground state. Because no single-crystal X-ray structure and no quantitative magnetic-susceptibility/µeff dataset are available, the geometries are treated as spectroscopically supported structural models rather than definitive crystallographic assignments. Gravimetric measurements at 298 and 308 K showed concentration-dependent inhibition, with the Cu(II) complex reaching a maximum reported inhibition efficiency of 97.8%. Langmuir analysis of the reported surface-coverage data gave R² values of 0.9914–0.9988 and ΔG°ads values of approximately −23.4 to −27.3 kJ mol⁻¹ , indicating spontaneous adsorption with mixed physical/electrostatic and more specific interfacial contributions. DFT-based FMO, MEP, NCI-RDG, ELF, and LOL analyses describe differences in the intrinsic electronic structures of the complexes, while no direct Fe-surface adsorption is inferred in the absence of explicit surface calculations.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Pavement systems are critical infrastructure assets subject to continuous degradation from mechanical loads and environmental factors. Conventional monitoring methods are often reactive and labor-intensive, failing to capture early-stage damage. Self-sensing composites (SSCs) offer a transformative solution by embedding piezoresistive sensing capabilities directly into the pavement structure, enabling simultaneous load-bearing and in-situ monitoring. This is achieved by incorporating conductive fillers, such as carbon fibers, nanotubes, or graphite, into cementitious or asphalt matrices, allowing the pavement to sense stress, strain, and damage by measuring changes in electrical resistivity. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the current state of SSC technology for pavement infrastructure. It systematically compiles and analyzes peer-reviewed studies on the mechanical and electrical properties of these functional materials. Key applications, including structural health monitoring (SHM), traffic detection, and weigh-in-motion (WIM), are discussed. Finally, the review identifies significant technical challenges, most notably signal interference from moisture and temperature, as well as high-level integration hurdles. Persisting research gaps are highlighted, and future directions are proposed, emphasizing the need for material optimization and the integration of artificial intelligence to bridge the gap from laboratory potential to full-scale field deployment.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Membrane distillation (MD) offers an energy-efficient way to desalination, but its commercial deployment is restricted by the limited availability of low-cost, highly hydrophobic membrane materials. This work aimed to engineer a superhydrophobic polystyrene (PS) nanofibrous membrane by impregnating the hierarchical surface roughness of a zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-8) into a carbon-nanotube scaffold in a single hybrid nanofiller (MWCNTs-ZIF-8), synthesized in situ and incorporated into electrospun PS fibers. Electrospinning conditions and filler loading were optimized, and the resulting neat and composite membranes were characterized via SEM, TEM, FTIR, XRD, BET, and 3D-laser scanning, and their performance was evaluated using a direct-contact MD (DCMD) test rig. The hybrid PS12-SDS/MWCNTs-ZIF-8 membrane was found to possess a superhydrophobic contact angle of 162°, the highest among all fabricated membranes, while the PS12-SDS/ZIF-8 membrane delivered the highest permeate flux (18.3 kg/m2.h, 32% above the neat PS12-SDS membrane). The MWCNTs-ZIF-8 membrane maintained > 99.5% salt rejection over 36 h of continuous operation, demonstrating its strong resistance to wetting. These results show that pairing a high-aspect-ratio carbon nanomaterial with a hydrophobic metal-organic framework within a single hybrid filler at low loading (≤ 0.6 wt%) is an effective design strategy for engineering durable, cost-efficient superhydrophobic membranes, positioning MWCNTs-ZIF-8/PS composite membranes as a promising advanced membrane material for membrane distillation.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Deep learning–based segmentation has become essential in computer-aided dental diagnosis and treatment planning. However, these models remain highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, like small and imperceptible changes in input images, which can drastically alter segmentation outputs and compromise clinical reliability. In this work, we present the first systematic study on adversarial vulnerability and robustness of deep learning models for panoramic dental X-ray segmentation. We curated a dataset of 995 panoramic images by combining 361 expert-annotated radiographs with 634 refined masks from the DENTEX 2023 challenge. Under identical training conditions, initially, we benchmarked 11 unique model variants, including five core architectures (Attention UNet, SegNet, Trans UNet, Vanilla UNet, and UNet++) and their corresponding ablations on training and preprocessing techniques. UNet++ emerged as the most practical backbone (clean IoU, Dice) and subjected to a suite of white-box attacks with FGSM, I-FGSM, PGD, and DeepFool across perturbation (). Our results reveal that even minimal perturbations caused large performance drops, such as at, IoU collapsed to 23.5% (0.851 to 0.649). To mitigate this fragility, we implemented a customized multi-attack adversarial defense strategy to ensure the model’s robustness, which preserved a modest clean-accuracy trade-off by increasing 14.9% (IoU 0.649 to 0.798) at and 12.5% at. Our qualitative and quantitative analyses demonstrate that the defended model produces more stable and anatomically consistent masks under attack and set the benchmark of adversarial robustness in dental image segmentation as an effective defense strategy for safety-critical clinical deployment.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Accurate forecasting of solar power generation plays a vital role in maximising energy output and ensuring grid stability in renewable energy systems. Conventional methods of forecasting can have a hard time modelling the intricate interactions of dynamic environmental factors, like variations in temperature, solar irradiance, and time-of-day effects. This paper proposes a Quantum Machine Learning (QML)-based model that is specifically focused on solar power forecasting and combines three approaches: Quantum Kernel Learning (QKL), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) and Linear Regression (LR). Using quantum-enhanced feature mapping and optimised quantum kernels, the model is able to deal with highly non-linear dependencies that are not easily modelled by classical approaches. The proposed approach is named the Hybrid Quantum Classical Model (HQCM) and compared to the classical KNN and LR models in terms of performance parameters. Training and testing were done using data obtained from solar power generation. The simulated results proved that the proposed HQCM can reduce Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 57.2% and 55.8%, respectively, with high stability and reliability predictions. The proposed model has achieved a good R2 of 0.999 with the Quantum K-Nearest Neighbours (QKNN) model and has an absolute error as high as 1.4 MW when the test dataset is recorded. Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) and residual distribution plots affirm that the quantum model errors are concentrated close to zero, while classical baselines exhibit much larger residual magnitudes. The proposed HQCM has the potential to be helpful in managing the energy grid and making the integration of solar power into smart grids easier. Future work will build on this to real-time optimisation of power grids while considering how other renewable energy sources can be optimised in this way.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Molar occlusion identification is a fundamental component of orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning. Conventional assessment using intraoral photographs relies on manual visual inspection, making it time-consuming and susceptible to inter-observer variability. Moreover, existing deep learning (DL)-based approaches either analyze the entire image without explicit anatomical localization or depend on manually defined regions of interest, thereby limiting clinical applicability. Accordingly, this study proposes a DL framework for molar occlusion classification. The proposed framework blends YOLO11-based anatomical localization with a Swin Transformer (Swin-T) for occlusion recognition. YOLO11 performs automatic instance segmentation to identify the molar region and eliminate non-diagnostic background content. The resulting prediction-guided molar crops are then processed by Swin-T, which learns discriminative representations of posterior occlusal relationships through hierarchical shifted-window attention and multiscale feature modeling. A dataset of 1101 intraoral images spanning five occlusion classes was used. The localization stage achieved a Dice coefficient of 96.82%. The developed framework attained classification accuracy of 98.17%, outperforming expert orthodontist assessment. Furthermore, the proposed framework outperformed well-established models, including ResNet50V2, DenseNet201, MobileNetV3-Large, EfficientNetV2-S, and vision transformer (ViT-B/16). Experimental results demonstrated perfect recall for Half Class II, Class III, and Half Class III, while maintaining strong predictive performance for Class I and Class II. Localization and explainability analyses confirmed that the framework consistently attended to clinically relevant posterior occlusal structures, affirming the anatomical plausibility of its predictions. These findings provide a promising foundation for automated molar occlusion assessment and suggest potential for future integration of DL-driven decision support into digital orthodontic workflows.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Recent advances in autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) are enabling new modes of planetary and orbital exploration. This paper presents a distributed neuro-adaptive sliding-mode formation control (DNASMFC) framework for multi-UAV quadrotor teams. DNASMFC combines the robustness of sliding-mode control with online neural adaptation to handle uncertainties, external disturbances, and modeling inaccuracies in the translational dynamics. A cascaded design is employed; a distributed, graph-based formation layer generates per-vehicle translational references based on DNASMFC, and a terminal sliding mode control (TSMC) drives the rotational axes to the commanded attitudes and thrust. The cascaded DNASMFC/TSMC is evaluate in MATLAB/Simulink, demonstrating stable formation keeping. Results indicate that DNASMFC/TSMC is a promising candidate for distributed exploration, and communication-relay swarms.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Swarm unmanned surface vehicle (USV) has become a promising solution for maritime security and defense activities. However, the complexity of continuous multi-target hunting presents significant challenges for multi-agent coordination in water environments. This study proposes an XAI-driven multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for swarm USVs to perform continuous multi-target hunting. The framework integrates multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (basic MAPPO and MAPPO-LSTM) for cooperative hunting policies with explainable AI (XAI) mechanisms to provide interpretable insights into swarm behaviors and decision strategies. Experimental results in a 3D simulation platform environment demonstrate that MAPPO-LSTM achieves superior interception performance, reducing mean time-to-capture and improving trajectory smoothness compared to the baseline MAPPO. Furthermore, the proposed XAI pipeline combines distance-based importance attribution, influence graph analysis, strategic clustering, and temporal dynamics evaluation to explain agent contributions, inter-agent dependencies, emergent strategies, and efficiency patterns. By providing multi-level interpretability, the framework enhances transparency, trust, and deployment readiness of swarm USVs in dynamic maritime defense scenarios.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Ammonia (NH3) is a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high hydrogen density, good storage characteristics, and existing global transport network. The catalytic decomposition of ammonia is an efficient method for generating hydrogen without CO2, but thermodynamic and kinetic constraints limit its use; it requires highly active and stable catalysts. Perovskite oxides have attracted significant research interest in recent years due to their compositional flexibility, tunable electronic structure, oxygen-vacancy chemistry, and strong metal–support interactions. This review highlights the relationships among crystal structure, oxygen non-stoichiometry, reducibility, defect formation, and catalytic performance of perovskite materials for ammonia decomposition, and summarizes recent developments in this field. The effects of A-site and B-site engineering on oxygen mobility and lattice distortion, surface basicity, catalyst reconstruction, and metal exsolution are systematically discussed. Reduction of the Ni and Co ions to the Ni0 and Co0 nanoparticles and their contribution to the improvement of catalytic activity and stability are of special interest. H2-TPR, XPS, XRD, TEM, SEM–EDS, and CO2-TPD are also explored to establish structure–property relationships to analyze the material in an advanced manner.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This paper introduces a practical solution for quadrotors under the effect of time delays. In actual control systems, time delays are inevitable because of the communication delays, heavy algorithm computations, and sensing delays. These delays have the potential to cause instability and deteriorate system performance if they are not appropriately addressed. In this paper, a Smith predictor is introduced to reduce the negative impacts of time delays and maintain closed-loop stability. However, the Smith predictor's performance may be hindered by modeling inaccuracies, and its effectiveness depends on a precise system model. A robust terminal sliding mode controller with a new sliding surface is suggested as a solution to this problem. Additionally, a fuzzy logic-based switching function is used in place of the discontinuous signum function to lessen noise impacts and chattering. Real-time results using a quadrotor platform show that the proposed methods can effectively control the platform with smaller tracking errors and reduced levels of chattering and noise. Also, it achieves at least a 27% improvement in the tracking error relative to other methods for the worst scenario.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Extrusion-based 3D printing of ultra-high-performance concrete (3DP-UHPC) combines the geometric freedom of additive manufacturing with high mechanical performance. But its implementation remains constrained by a narrow processing range, anisotropy, cost, and binder-related environmental burdens. This review critically synthesizes advances in mixture design and sustainability, focusing on how particle packing, water-to-binder ratio, supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), fibers, nanomaterials, and chemical admixtures govern rheology, extrusion stability, structural build-up, interlayer bonding, and hardened performance. The evidence shows that printability cannot be optimized through isolated constituent adjustments. Superplasticizers must reduce pumping resistance without delaying structural rebuilding and viscosity-modifying agents improve cohesion without impairing extrusion. Fiber dosage and dispersion must enhance crack bridging without promoting blockage or anisotropy and deposition time and surface condition must preserve interlayer integrity. SCMs, low-clinker binders, industrial by-products, recycled fibers, and alternative aggregates can reduce environmental impact, although their benefits must be verified against printability, strength, shrinkage, durability, print-failure rate, and life-cycle performance. Standardized reporting, data-driven mixture proportioning, in-process monitoring, life-cycle assessment, and performance-based acceptance criteria are identified as priorities for translating 3DP-UHPC from laboratory development to reliable structural deployment.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Hydrogenation of guaiacol, a model compound of lignin-derived bio-oil, coupled with internally produced hydrogen from glycerol aqueous-phase reforming (APR) over Raney Ni, was investigated to evaluate the role of reactor operation on hydrogen availability and product distribution. Reaction engineering strategies, including batch, semi-batch, and continuous glycerol feeding modes, were systematically compared. Full saturation of the guaiacol aromatic ring was achieved with a combined liquid-phase selectivity to cyclohexanol and cyclohexanone reaching 90% when both guaiacol and glycerol conversion reached 99%. A previously unreported benzene formation pathway via cyclohexanol dehydration and dehydrogenation was identified, leading to a benzene selectivity of 13.8% under hydrogen-deficient conditions. This study shows that hydrogen availability is highly dynamic and controlled by both glycerol consumption and the feeding strategy, governing the transition between hydrogenation and dehydrogenation pathways. Increasing glycerol input in batch mode did not significantly improve selectivity to oxygen-free products due to catalyst site competition and inefficient hydrogen utilization. In contrast, semi-batch and continuous feeding maintained lower glycerol concentrations, leading to sustained hydrogen production and mitigation of undesired dehydrogenation reactions. Slightly improved hydrogenation performance with a liquid-phase selectivity of 69.4% to cyclohexanol was achieved with continuous glycerol feeding. Besides, guaiacol hydrogenation with glycerol APR as the hydrogen source was comparable to that using 8.5 bar external hydrogen, which resulted in an 88% combined liquid-phase selectivity to cyclohexanol and cyclohexanone. These findings demonstrate that reactor operation is a key design parameter affecting hydrogen supply and needs to be carefully considered in tandem APR-hydrogenation systems for biomass upgrading.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Geomagnetic anomaly sensing provides a noncontact approach to assessing buried steel pipelines, yet weak defect signatures are often masked by environmental noise and uncertainty in detector orientation. This study introduces an integrated workflow that combines empirical mode decomposition with a detrended fluctuation analysis-based mode selection for adaptive denoising and employs the modulus of the magnetic gradient tensor for orientation robust localization, supported by a dipole forward model that links defect parameters to the measured field. In simulations with additive white noise (input SNR 5 dB), the EMD plus DFA pipeline achieves the strongest reconstruction among common baselines, increasing output SNR to 19.45 dB with RMSE 0.329 nT and outperforming moving average and wavelet filtering. Field trials on a Q235 steel pipeline (inner diameter about 325 mm, wall thickness 5 mm) with a 1.5 m sensor standoff and 1 kHz sampling confirm practical gains. The MGTM response forms a sharp, well-localized peak within 0.12 m of the ground truth defect, whereas single-axis gradients yield broader, less stable responses under changes in survey azimuth. The results demonstrate that coupling EMD with DFA and MGTM improves detectability and positional accuracy without excavation, using only surface measurements suitable for routine integrity management.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This study develops an interpretable data-centric machine learning paradigm to predict the compressive strength of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) with recycled concrete powder (RCP). Given limited experimental data, an experimental dataset of 80 samples was augmented with 300 synthesized concrete mix designs to improve the model. We evaluated the performance of two machine learning methods using extreme learning machine (ELM) and CatBoost, employing three different data strategies: experimental only (M1), synthetic only (M2), and combined (M3). Our results showed that CatBoost in the combined strategy (M3) outperformed the competition with an R2 of 0.968 and the best error metrics in the test phase. To demonstrate the feature contributions, we used SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and found that the most important features explaining compressive strength included cement, steel fibers, and water. Our proposed method demonstrates that combining generative data with explainable machine learning significantly improves both predictive performance and transparency, suggesting potential for designing and optimizing concrete mix recipes for sustainable UHPC.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This paper presents a carbon-aware hierarchical dispatch approach for the joint scheduling of transmission, distribution, and microgrid systems. The framework considers operation of complex multi-layer power networks, wherein independent optimization of each layer can give rise to infeasible and inconsequential boundary exchanges, contradictory carbon calculation, and suboptimal use of distributed flexibility. The problem is cast as a three-level optimization. At the transmission level, generation scheduling and locational carbon intensity for the bulk power system are established. At the distribution level, dispatch choices synchronize distributed generation and responsive demand. At the level of microgrid, local energy management is carried out subject to explicit carbon budget constraints. To address the tightly coupled integer nonlinear optimization problem in a decentralized way, a tri-level alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with adaptive penalty updating is designed. As a dynamic variable, the carbon emission intensity coordinates the layers to ensure emissions are tracked consistently. For distribution network constraints, SOCR is employed. Simulation studies are conducted on an integrated transmission–distribution–microgrid test system. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework, relative to uncoordinated operation with the same carbon constraints, reduces operating costs from 501,840 to 468,940 USD/day through effective coordination of multi-layer resources. Compared to a coordinated baseline without carbon constraints, the carbon-aware framework increases operating costs by approximately 13.7% (412,480 → 468,940 USD/day) while achieving substantial emissions reductions from 8240 to 4630 tCO2/day (43.8% reduction). Wind curtailment is reduced from 285 to 142 MWh, and microgrid carbon budget violations are eliminated. The proposed method yields a result close to the convex relaxation of the centralized MISOCP solution (which serves as a practical benchmark within our modeling framework) with cost and emission gaps of 0.36% and 0.70%, respectively, and computation time is reduced from 8420 s to 598 s. These findings demonstrate that the architecture can effectively enable coordinated low-carbon dispatch across multi-layer power systems at a quantifiable economic cost that is justified by significant environmental benefits.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: This paper offers a methodology for achieving parameter identification for a single-area power system. The accuracy of parameter identification is essential because system characteristics may change due to equipment aging, environmental and operational variations, and insufficient maintenance. Additionally, some physical parameters cannot be measured directly, which requires a more accurate mathematical model. Therefore, parameter estimation is needed to reduce the gap between the simulation model and the actual system and improve the accuracy of system analysis. In this study, the Cloud Drift Optimizer (CDO), a recently developed metaheuristic algorithm that has not yet been investigated in power system, is applied for parameter identification in a single-area power system. To evaluate its effectiveness, CDO is compared with the Flood Algorithm (FLA), Artificial Rabbits Optimization (ARO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Genetic Algorithm (GA) using the same identification framework. The results demonstrate that CDO achieves the best performance compared with the other algorithms in terms of the considered error indices. The findings confirm that the proposed CDO-based approach is a promising and effective technique for parameter identification in power system studies.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Governments are racing to scale low-carbon hydrogen, yet like-for-like evidence on the coverage of enacted hydrogen production-policy instruments remains scarce. To address this gap, this study develops a transparent benchmark that maps twelve enacted measures into four pillars: Strategy/Targets, Funding & Market, Standards & Certification, and Permitting & Administration. Countries are compared using two complementary metrics: Hamming distance, which captures differences in the presence or absence of individual instruments, and an (Formula presented) ​-norm distance based on normalized pillar-level coverage scores. A sample-relative distance-to-frontier metric further expresses the share of peer-frontier policy features not yet enacted. The framework measures the enactment and structural coverage of production-policy instruments; it does not directly evaluate implementation quality, policy effectiveness, the financial magnitude of support, or causal effects on hydrogen deployment. Applied to six selected benchmark countries and Saudi Arabia, the coverage-based findings are consistent across methods: Germany records the highest composite coverage score (0.854), followed by Australia (0.833), Spain (0.771), the United Kingdom (0.750), the United States (0.688), China (0.625), and Saudi Arabia (0.312). Pairwise proximity patterns are stable, the Hamming and (Formula presented) ​ distance families show strong agreement (Spearman correlation ≈ 0.76), and the (Formula presented) ​-based rankings remain robust to ±20% pillar reweighting (Spearman ≥ 0.975). Based on the instrument-coverage gaps identified for Saudi Arabia, the priority measures are to establish a national certification/guarantees-of-origin system with auditable life-cycle assessment and monitoring, reporting and verification; complete the standards framework; introduce state-backed offtake and production-linked operating support; and implement fast-track permitting with a referenced safety code. Overall, the framework provides a replicable, decision-oriented baseline for comparing and periodically tracking enacted hydrogen production-policy instrument coverage across countries.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Deep-learning-based few-shot synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection has demonstrated considerable potential in scenarios with limited annotated samples and dynamically emerging ship categories, closely matching the practical requirements of maritime surveillance and intelligent SAR image interpretation. However, existing methods often overlook challenging negative proposals and the incomplete annotation problem inherent in few-shot learning. In complex offshore and inshore scenes, negative proposals contain either difficult background regions caused by sea clutter, port facilities, and strong scattering interference, or unlabeled ship targets resulting from missing annotations. Existing methods struggle to distinguish between these two types of proposals. Ignoring challenging negatives prevents the detector from learning precise decision boundaries between ships and complex backgrounds, whereas treating unlabeled ships as background introduces erroneous gradients during backpropagation and degrades detection performance. To address these issues, we introduce uncertainty as a measure of proposal reliability and propose two complementary components: uncertainty-guided proposal separation (UGPS) and uncertainty-aware discriminative gradient refocusing (UADGR). UGPS jointly exploits proposal uncertainty and intersection-over-union (IoU) to separate challenging negatives and confusing negatives from the negative proposal set, thereby preserving informative hard backgrounds while identifying potential unlabeled ships. Subsequently, UADGR combines proposal uncertainty with feature dissimilarity to a background prototype to adaptively regulate their training gradients. Specifically, higher weights are assigned to challenging negatives to improve discrimination between ships and complex background interference, whereas lower weights are assigned to confusing negatives to suppress erroneous supervision introduced by missing ship annotations. Extensive experiments on SRSDD-v1.0 demonstrate consistent improvements over existing few-shot detection approaches across different data splits and shot settings, while additional results on SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 further confirm the generalization of the proposed method.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Casing wear is a major well-integrity risk in directional drilling due to repeated sliding contact between the casing inner wall and the drill pipe tool joint (TJ). The paper analyses wear in API 5CT L-80 and P110 steel grades using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to identify differences in their behaviour under representative operational parameters. A three-dimensional explicit contact model is developed in ANSYS Workbench LS-DYNA and implemented using Archard’s wear law, which calculates wear depth and related parameters from local contact pressure and sliding distance. Once validated against reference wear data for a baseline L-80 case (115 RPM at 1000 N), the model is used in a parametric analysis to assess side loads (1000 N to 1400 N) and rotational speeds (115 RPM to 207 RPM). The findings indicate that wear increases with both normal load and speed, with normal load having a greater influence. Under identical parameters, the materials produce different levels of wear in the worst-case scenario ( at 115 RPM and 1400 N, P110 has ~35% lower wear than L-80) and a much smaller difference (i.e., at 207 RPM and 1000 N, P110 has ~5% lower wear than L-80). Consequently, upgrading to P110 in high-load environments with severe contact will yield the greatest benefit from upgraded casing, thereby providing an economic tool for grade selection and wear-risk evaluations via calibrated FEA models.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: Buildings account for nearly 40% of global energy demand, with 20–40% attributed to space heating and cooling, making roofs a critical target for improving thermal performance. This study proposes an integrated sustainability assessment and machine learning (ML) framework to evaluate and predict green roof performance under subtropical climatic conditions. Experimental data on energy storage in roof slabs, exergy variation during space heating and cooling, and daily electricity cost savings were analyzed using combined energy–exergy–economic indicators. ML models, including Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), achieved high predictive accuracy (R² > 0.95) with prediction errors below 5%. Global sensitivity analysis identified space cooling electricity savings as the dominant factor, contributing approximately 49% of total sensitivity, followed by exergy performance (31%). SHAP-based explainability showed that energy storage parameters governed ML predictions, accounting for up to 69% of total SHAP contribution. Experimental results demonstrated that macroencapsulated PCM-integrated roofs reduced indoor temperatures by up to 7.3°C and mitigated heat gain by 51.35%, with a cost recovery period of 5.7 years. The proposed framework offers a robust, interpretable, and computationally efficient decision-support tool for climate-resilient green roof design.

mods:mods.mods:abstract: The increased world population demands that renewable and alternative sources of energy that can meet present and future energy demands be explored at large scale. Energy scientists are working to harvest two of the most abundant resources on earth i.e. water through hydrogen production and sunlight through PV solar cells. Hydrogen production is a complicated, expensive and time-consuming process. Direct conversion of sunlight into electricity through PV solar cells is a simple, cost-effective and efficient process. The current photovoltaic solar cell market is dominated by silicon-based materials, which are expensive, toxic and difficult to install. To produce low-cost, eco-friendly and efficient PV solar cells, various techniques such as heterojunction formation, photosensitization and doping are being employed. Alkali doping has been used widely, but their results are not promising for commercial application and their toxic nature is an additional disadvantage. Although there is limited research on bismuth doping, it is considered a potential candidate for PV doping, as it enhances the stability, efficiency and tunability of electronic as well as optical properties. Bismuth doping increases crystal size, narrows the band gap, reduces synthesis temperature and stabilizes the PV material for long-term use. These properties lead to higher power conversion efficiency (max. 17.4%). Based on inexpensive, relatively less toxic nature, strong spin orbit coupling constant, large ionic radii etc. of bismuth, in this article, we present critical analysis of changes in band gap and power conversion efficiency (PCE) induced by Bi doping, which plays a key role in enhancing photovoltaic cell efficiency. This review further elaborates the role of bismuth in various PV materials, including perovskite, silicon and chalcopyrite, addresses current challenges and future prospects and provides a gateway to enhance PV cell efficiency through bismuth doping.
